transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my mind just won’t hold onto things anymore. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—and the words and numbers just scatter on me.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
Most days, yes. I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. Even when my wife is being kind and talking to me, I feel like I’m down at the bottom of a well.
How long have you been noticing this trouble holding onto words and numbers—did it start around the same time as the low mood, or before it?
About three weeks now. It started after my older sister died—ever since then, I’ve had trouble keeping hold of words and numbers.
Before your sister passed away three weeks ago, had you noticed any similar trouble with memory, concentration, or word-finding, even in a milder form?
No, not that I can recall. Before then, I could write those program notes without any trouble—now I sit there and the words and numbers just won’t stay with me.
Besides missing your sister, have you been feeling worthless, excessively guilty, or like you've failed as a person in other areas of your life?
I’m not sure. I’ve been feeling very low, but I don’t know if I’d call myself worthless or say I’ve failed at everything.

Besides trouble finding words and numbers, have you noticed any problems with things like getting confused about the day or date, losing your way in familiar places, or forgetting how to do routine tasks you've done for years?
No, I haven’t noticed things like that. I’m not getting lost or forgetting how to do things I’ve always done.
Do you notice this heavy, low feeling even during moments when you're not thinking about your sister—like when you're focused on something else entirely, such as work or a hobby?

Yes. Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. Even if I’m focused on something else, or my wife is being kind and talking to me, I still feel like I’m down at the bottom of a well.
Since your sister passed away, have you been having intrusive, unwanted memories or images of her death, or nightmares about it, that come to you even when you don't want them to?
I’m not sure what counts as intrusive. I do think about her, but I can’t really say I’ve been having unwanted images or nightmares about her death.
